order_description: Respiratory assist device, bi-level pressure capability, without backup rate feature, used with noninvasive interface, e.g., nasal or facial mask (intermittent assist device with continuous positive airway pressure device)

candidates.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea

selection_reason: The order is for an E0470 bi-level device, and the patient has severe OSA (AHI 32 on attended PSG with 227 events). L33718 covers E0470 for OSA when E0601 was tried and proven ineffective despite proper mask fitting and appropriate pressure settings. The record documents CPAP intolerance after nasal pillow and full-face mask refitting and pressure adjustment, with use on 11 of 30 nights averaging 2.8 hours. The sleep test meets the AHI of 15 or more criterion, and the in-person evaluation and device instruction are documented. L33800 addresses CSA, hypoventilation, or COPD-related chronic respiratory failure, which the record does not show; the desaturation is explained by obstructive events. L33405 covers sleep testing, not device coverage.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has an in-person clinical evaluation by the treating practitioner prior to the sleep test to assess the beneficiary for obstructive sleep apnea.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test was the attended Type I polysomnogram on 2025-11-03 (R24). The record shows no in-person evaluation to assess for OSA before that date: the 2025-01-22 general examination (R21, R78) does not mention sleep apnea or sleep symptoms. The OSA evaluations that do exist come after the test (2026-03-06 sleep medicine consultation R25; 2026-03-31 otolaryngology visit with physical exam R26, R82). The policy also requires a new initial in-person evaluation when switching from an E0601 used for more than 3 months, and the 2026-03-31 otolaryngology visit with physical exam may serve that purpose. However, the record does not state that the encounters were in person or identify which practitioner is the treating practitioner for this order, so the requirement cannot be confirmed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary has a sleep test that meets either of the following criteria (1 or 2): 1. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 15 events per hour with a minimum of 30 events; or 2. The AHI or RDI is greater than or equal to 5 and less than or equal to 14 events per hour with a minimum of 10 events and documentation of excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia, or hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.
criteria.explanation: Alternative 1 applies. The attended in-laboratory polysomnography on 2025-11-04/05 reports an AHI of 32 events per hour, which is at or above 15, with 227 events over 7.1 hours of sleep, which is above the minimum of 30 events. Alternative 2 is not needed.

criteria.policy_text: The beneficiary and/or their caregiver has received instruction from the supplier of the device in the proper use and care of the equipment.
criteria.explanation: A home CPAP unit is listed (R19) and device download data show use (R43, R50), but the record contains no documentation that the supplier instructed the beneficiary or caregiver in the proper use and care of the equipment.

criteria.policy_text: An E0601 has been tried and proven ineffective based on a therapeutic trial conducted in either a facility or in a home setting. Ineffective means documented failure to meet therapeutic goals using an E0601 despite optimal therapy (proper mask selection and fitting and appropriate pressure settings).
criteria.explanation: The beneficiary had a home trial of CPAP starting 2025-11-30. Despite mask refitting (nasal pillows, then full-face mask), heated humidification and pressure adjustment, the device download shows use on only 11 of the last 30 nights, averaging 2.8 hours on nights used, which fails the adherence goal of 4 or more hours on 70% of nights. Residual AHI on CPAP is 3 per hour. The sleep medicine physician documents CPAP intolerance despite these optimization steps.

criteria.policy_text: A sleep test (Type I, II, III, IV, Other) that meets the Medicare requirements for a valid sleep test as outlined in NCD 240.4.1 and the applicable A/B MAC LCD and Billing and Coding article.
criteria.explanation: The sleep test is an attended in-laboratory polysomnography, which is the Type I facility-based study the policy requires. The written report (R76) gives AHI, sleep time and oxygen nadir. The record does not itemize every NCD 240.4.1 validity element, but the test type and reported results match the required study type.

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test results meet the coverage criteria in effect for the date of service of the claim for the PAP device.
criteria.explanation: The AHI of 32 events per hour with 227 events over 7.1 hours of sleep meets the AHI threshold of 15 or more with at least 30 events in the first alternative of the sleep test criteria (see I.B).

criteria.policy_text: The sleep test is ordered by the beneficiary's treating practitioner.
criteria.explanation: The polysomnography encounter (R24) is listed with a sleep center technologist and the reason 'Suspected obstructive sleep apnea', and the report (R76) does not name the ordering practitioner. The record does not document that the treating practitioner ordered the sleep test.

decision_explanation: No applicable criterion is clearly not met. Criterion II.D (failed E0601 trial despite optimal therapy) and the sleep test criteria (I.B, Sleep Tests.1 and .3) are met. Criteria I.A (in-person evaluation to assess for OSA, with the switch-from-E0601 evaluation not confirmed as in person), I.C (supplier instruction in equipment use not documented), and Sleep Tests.4 (ordering practitioner for the sleep test not documented) lack the needed evidence, so the request cannot be decided as covered or denied on this record. FDA status of the test and the provider's Medicare or state compliance were excluded as regulatory or administrative items, and the continued-coverage, oxygen, replacement, accessory, refill and entering-Medicare sections do not apply to this initial E0470 order.
